_gr = np.meshgrid(*[np.linspace(*P[k].prange, 21) for k in MV], indexing="ij")

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Low-pH viral inactivation is Step 6 of the A-Mab drug substance process and the first
dedicated viral clearance step of the purification train. The Protein A eluate is titrated
to a low pH, held for a defined time at controlled temperature, and neutralised before
cation exchange chromatography (Step 7). Enveloped virus is inactivated by acid
denaturation of the viral envelope. The step contributes `{python} f"{vi_xmulv:.2f}"` log₁₀ to the cumulative
XMuLV clearance of `{python} f"{cum_xmulv:.2f}"` log₁₀ claimed for the process, which is
the largest single contribution of the `{python} n_vc_steps` credited steps (@tbl-vc). The
studies were
executed on a qualified small-scale spiking model under the approved protocol PCP-006. They
follow the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011], the enhanced development
approach of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11], and the viral safety framework of
ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a].

The step has `{python} n_par` parameters, `{python} n_mv` of which were characterized in a
multivariate design (@tbl-params).
Inactivation pH is classified as a critical process parameter. Hold time and temperature
are well-controlled critical process parameters, and A-Mab concentration is a general
process parameter. A two-level screening design of `{python} n_scr` runs identified pH, hold time and
temperature as active on the log reduction factor, and a face-centred central composite
design of `{python} n_rsm` runs provided the response-surface models. The screening
design identifies the active factors. The response-surface model is the predictive model
and the basis of the operating region.

Across the characterized ranges the pool aggregate stays below `{python} f"{agg_hi:.0f}"` %
and the acidic charge variants below `{python} f"{acv_hi:.0f}"` %, at every combination of
the factors studied. The log reduction factor meets the required step contribution of
`{python} f"{lrf_lo:.2f}"` log₁₀ everywhere except at one corner of the characterized
cube, where the highest pH is combined with the shortest hold and the lowest temperature.
At that corner, `{python} n_below` executed runs returned log reduction factors below the
required contribution, the lowest of them `{python} f"{lrf_corner_min:.2f}"` log₁₀. That
corner is excluded from the operating region. The normal operating ranges lie well inside
the region that remains, and at their least favourable corner the model predicts
`{python} f"{lrf_nor:.2f}"` log₁₀, a margin of
`{python} f"{lrf_nor_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ over the requirement.

At commercial scale the cumulative XMuLV clearance has a mean of
`{python} f"{xmulv_mean:.2f}"` log₁₀ against a requirement of at least
`{python} f"{xmulv_req:.1f}"` log₁₀, a margin of `{python} f"{xmulv_margin:.2f}"`
log₁₀, and a one-sided Cpk of `{python} f"{xmulv_cpk:.2f}"` (@tbl-cap). It is the
tightest of the attributes this step governs, and the capability rests on the other
credited steps as well as on this one. The study recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations
during execution. Both were investigated and dispositioned as retained, and neither altered
a parameter classification or the reported operating region.

No clearance of non-enveloped virus is claimed for this step, and its MVM contribution is
reported as `{python} f"{vi_mvm:.1f}"` log₁₀ (@tbl-vc). The cumulative XMuLV claim also
rests on the anion exchange step (PCR-008) and on the small-virus retentive filtration step
(PCR-009), which act by different mechanisms. The step assures a defined enveloped-virus
inactivation increment and a bounded product quality cost. It does not by itself assure
the viral safety of the drug substance. This report rolls up into PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose primary mechanism of action is
antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. It is produced by fed-batch cell culture and
purified by a platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation
exchange chromatography, anion exchange chromatography, small-virus retentive filtration
and ultrafiltration with diafiltration (Steps 5–10). The train is the one described in the
A-Mab case study [@amab2009], and this report covers the second of its downstream steps.

The step is a batch hold. The Protein A eluate is titrated with acid to the target pH in a
mixed vessel, held for the target time under temperature control, and then neutralised to
the pH required by the cation exchange load. Inactivation of enveloped virus proceeds by
acid-driven denaturation of the envelope glycoproteins, which is a kinetic process. Its
extent therefore depends on the pH reached, on how long the material is held there, and on
the temperature at which it is held. The same conditions act on the antibody, where partial
acid unfolding produces high molecular weight species (HMW) and asparagine deamidation over
the hold raises the acidic charge variant level. The step is a balance between these two
effects, and characterizing it means bounding both.

The step sets the XMuLV clearance credited to it in the modular viral safety claim
(@tbl-cqa). It does not form the aggregate or the charge variant attributes, which are
established in the production bioreactor (PCR-003). It adds to both, and
aggregate is subsequently reduced at cation exchange (PCR-007). Clearance of host cell
protein by precipitation at low pH is not claimed here, since it is not reliably
predictable across feed states.

## Objectives

The objectives of the characterization were as follows.

(i) Quantify the relationship between the operating parameters of the step and the XMuLV
log reduction factor, the pool aggregate level and the acidic charge variant level.
(ii) Define the multivariate operating region within which all three responses meet their
acceptance criteria.
(iii) Establish the proven acceptable range of each parameter for each attribute it
governs, both with the other parameters held fixed and with them varying within their
normal operating ranges.
(iv) Classify each parameter against the decision logic of SOP-4001.
(v) Justify the ranges to be run in Stage 2 and the contribution this step makes to the
control strategy for the drug substance.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is a Stage 1 process design activity in the sense of the lifecycle approach to
process validation [@fda2011]. Its record is the evidence that the commercial ranges were
established from designed experiments on a qualified model, and not from a small number of
engineering runs. The enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 and the risk framework of ICH
Q9 apply throughout, and the parameter classification treats criticality as a continuum
[@ichq9]. ICH Q11 frames the link from the studies to the control strategy [@ichq11].

Viral safety is evaluated under ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. That guideline sets the framework
used here in three ways. Clearance is claimed on a modular basis, so that each step is
studied independently and the increments are summed. Clearance data are generated at small
scale with a deliberately spiked feed, because virus cannot be introduced into a
manufacturing process. Steps are credited only where the mechanism of removal or
inactivation is understood and the operating conditions that deliver it are controlled. The
A-Mab case study provides the process model, the attribute framework and the risk
methodology [@amab2009].

This report is one document of a cross-referenced package. Its risk basis, its paired
protocol and the report it rolls up into are listed in @tbl-related.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The low-pH hold is a platform step with a long performance history. It has been used to
manufacture three previously licensed humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab),
and its operating conditions have remained essentially unchanged across those products and
throughout A-Mab development. The mechanism of inactivation is not product specific, since it depends on the pH and
temperature of the solution and on the exposure time, so the knowledge gained on the
platform transfers directly to A-Mab. Characterization therefore
confirms and bounds the step for this molecule. It is not a search for the operating
conditions.

Prior knowledge sets a clear mechanistic expectation, and the study was designed to test
it. Log reduction should rise as pH falls, as the hold lengthens and as the temperature
rises, because all three increase the extent of acid denaturation over the hold. Aggregate
should rise with hold time and with temperature for the same reason acting on the antibody,
and should be largely independent of pH within the narrow band studied. Acidic charge
variants should rise with hold time, since deamidation accumulates with exposure. If the
data contradict any of these expectations, the platform justification for the step would
have to be re-examined.

The same prior knowledge sets the edges of the characterized ranges. The low edge of the pH
range sits above the region in which antibody precipitation has been observed on the
platform, so that precipitation could not confound the study. The high edge sits above the
pH at which inactivation of enveloped virus has been shown to be reliable within a short
hold, which is what makes the upper part of the pH range the interesting part. The hold
time range extends to `{python} f"{hold_ratio:.0f}"` times its lower edge, and the
temperature range spans the controlled room-temperature band available in the manufacturing
suite.

## Quality attributes in scope

The step governs `{python} n_gov` drug substance attributes, and they differ widely in
criticality (@tbl-cqa). Criticality was assigned by the Tool #1 method of the case study
(impact multiplied by uncertainty), and attributes scoring high or very high are called
critical [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(GOV_KEYS))
```

: Quality attributes governed by the low-pH viral inactivation step, with acceptance
criteria and criticality. {#tbl-cqa}

XMuLV clearance is the attribute this step sets. It is of very high criticality, and its
acceptance criterion is cumulative across the credited steps, which is why the criterion
in @tbl-cqa is larger than any single step can deliver. Aggregate is of high criticality
and carries the highest Tool #1 score of the three. It is formed upstream, added to here,
and polished downstream, so this step's obligation is to bound its own increment. Acidic
charge variants are of very low criticality, and the attribute is carried in scope because
the hold adds to the level formed upstream and that increment has to be bounded.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

The scope of the study was set by RA-001, which ranked every parameter of the step by its
potential impact on a CQA and by its potential to interact with other parameters. The
ranking sent `{python} n_mv` of them to multivariate study. Inactivation pH
carries the largest expected effect on log reduction and the narrowest operating band. Hold
time drives log reduction, aggregate and deamidation at once, which makes it the parameter
most likely to force a compromise. Temperature acts on the same kinetics as hold time and
was expected to interact with it.

A-Mab concentration was assigned to univariate assessment. Its plausible mechanism is a
matrix effect on the acid titration and on the local ionic environment, which prior
knowledge places well below the three kinetic factors in magnitude, and no interaction with
them was expected. Studying it one factor at a time over its full range was judged
sufficient. The ranges taken forward for the multivariate factors are wider than their
normal operating ranges (@tbl-params), which is deliberate. A range that only covers the
control band cannot
distinguish a robust parameter from an unstudied one, and it leaves no room for movement
within the design space later in the lifecycle.

# Materials and methods

The step was executed on a qualified scale-down model under the controlled documents listed
in @tbl-sop. The procedures cover model qualification, the design and analysis of the DoE
studies, the operation of the step itself, and the parameter classification logic (SOP-4001)
applied in the classification section below.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=VIRAL_INACT_SOP_REFS, amvs=VIRAL_INACT_AMV_REFS))
```

: Controlled documents and validated analytical methods applied to this step. {#tbl-sop}

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The scale-down model is a jacketed, mixed vessel operated with the same pH, temperature and
hold profile as the commercial step. The variables that govern the inactivation are
scale-independent, because the hold is a homogeneous liquid-phase reaction with no
transport limitation. The model therefore reproduces the commercial step by matching
the acid titration path, the target pH, the hold time, the temperature and the
neutralisation, and by using representative Protein A eluate as the feed. Mixing was set to
give the same time to pH homogeneity as the commercial vessel, so that no part of the
batch experiences a shorter effective hold than the record states.

Qualification followed SOP-1001, under which the model was operated at the target
conditions and its input and output attributes were compared with the commercial-scale batch
data (pool aggregate, acidic charge variants, protein concentration and step recovery). No
difference of practical consequence was found, and the model is accepted as
representative for the definition of operating ranges. Clearance claims rest on the same
qualification with one addition required by ICH Q5A(R2). Virus can only be introduced at
small scale, so the spiking model must also be shown to hold the feed matrix, the spike
volume and the neutralisation step within the limits under which the clearance is claimed
[@ichq5a]. The spike volume was kept small enough that the acid titration path of the run
was set by the eluate and not by the spike.

Replicate centre-point runs were included in both designs, `{python} cp_scr` in the
screening design and `{python} cp_rsm` in the response-surface design. They provide the
pure-error estimate against which lack of fit is tested, and they also give a direct
measure of the reproducibility of the model and the assays.

## Operation

Each run started from a representative Protein A eluate held at the platform target
concentration. The eluate was titrated with acid to the run's target pH under mixing, and
the pH was confirmed by an independent probe (a second, separately calibrated instrument)
before the hold clock was started. The material was then held at the run's target temperature for the run's target time, sampled,
and neutralised. Samples for infectivity titration were taken from the spiked hold vessel
immediately before neutralisation, and product quality samples were taken from the
neutralised pool.

Inputs other than the three factors were controlled to their platform specifications and
were not varied. Buffer identity, acid and base titrant concentration, vessel geometry and
mixing rate all fall into this group. These are identity and quality controlled inputs, and
they are verified at use. They were not characterized in this study.

## Analytical methods

XMuLV infectivity was determined by TCID50 titration under AMV-3017. The method has a
validated intermediate precision of `{python} f"{amv_3017_precision:.2f}"` log₁₀, a
quantitation limit of `{python} f"{amv_3017_loq:.1f}"` log₁₀ TCID50/mL and an accuracy of
`{python} f"{amv_3017_accuracy:.0f}"` %. Method validation attributes
`{python} pct(amv_3017_var_frac)` of the total observed variance in a reported titre to the
assay. The log reduction factor is the difference between the titre of the spiked load and
the titre of the post-hold sample, so a reported log reduction factor carries the
uncertainty of two titrations and not of one.

Pool aggregate was determined by SEC-HPLC under AMV-3011 and reported as a percentage of
high molecular weight species. Acidic charge variants were determined by icIEF under
AMV-3013 and reported as a percentage of the total charge variant profile. The techniques,
analytes and reportable values are summarized in Appendix D. Full method performance is
held in the validation reports referenced in @tbl-sop, and is not reproduced here.

## Sampling plan

Every run was sampled twice for infectivity, once from the spiked load before acidification
and once from the hold vessel at the end of the hold. Product quality samples were drawn
from the neutralised pool of every run and assayed for aggregate and charge variants. The
centre-point runs were sampled in the same way as the factorial and axial runs, so that the
replicate estimate of variance covers sampling and assay variation as well as run-to-run
process variation.

## Statistical methods

Factors were coded so that the centre of each characterization range is zero and the two
edges are minus one and plus one. The screening design was analysed by ordinary least
squares (OLS) with all main effects and all two-factor interactions, and an effect is
reported as twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in the response across the
full range of that factor. The response-surface design was analysed with the full quadratic
model in the same factors. The significance level is 0.05 throughout.

Model adequacy was judged on four grounds. The coefficient of determination and its
adjusted form measure how much of the observed variation the model explains. The predicted
form, computed from the PRESS statistic, measures how well the model predicts a run that
was left out of the fit, and it is the most demanding of the three measures. The overall F test
determines whether the model explains more than noise. Lack of fit is tested by comparing
the residual variation that the model cannot explain with the pure error estimated from the
replicate centre points, and a significant lack of fit would mean that the fitted form is
too simple for the data. A factor with no significant term in either analysis is treated as
having no demonstrated effect over the range studied.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches with every parameter of the train drawn inside
its normal operating range, and is reported as a one-sided Cpk against the acceptance
criterion of each attribute.

# Study design

The design resolves the kinetic factors in two stages. The screening stage determines
which factors and interactions are active, and the response-surface stage adds the
curvature terms needed to describe the region and to predict inside it. The factors, their
set-points, their normal operating ranges and the ranges characterized are given in
@tbl-params, and the coded letters used throughout the results are given in @tbl-legend.

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

The characterization ranges in @tbl-params are the knowledge space of the step, and each
was justified before execution. The pH range is the widest of them relative to its normal
operating range, because pH is the parameter with the largest expected effect and the
narrowest control band, and because the upper part of the range is where the step is
expected to lose effectiveness. The hold time range starts at the shortest hold that would
be accepted and extends well past the control band, so that a curtailed hold and a
prolonged hold caused by a downstream delay are both covered. The temperature range spans
the full controlled room-temperature band. A-Mab concentration was studied across the whole
range over which the Protein A eluate is delivered (PCR-005), which is why its
characterization range and its normal operating range coincide.

## Screening design

The screening study was a two-level full factorial in the three multivariate factors with
`{python} cp_scr` centre points, giving `{python} n_scr` runs in total. A full factorial
was chosen over a fraction because the factors are few enough that every two-factor
interaction (AB, AC and BC) can be estimated independently of the main effects. The design
resolves every main effect and every two-factor interaction, and the centre points allow
curvature to be detected as an aggregate departure from the plane. The runs were executed
in randomised order, and the full matrix and the measured responses are given in
Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study was a face-centred central composite design in the same
factors, with `{python} n_ax` axial runs added to the `{python} 2 ** n_fac` factorial
corners and `{python} cp_rsm` centre points, giving `{python} n_rsm` runs. The axial points
sit on the faces of the cube (the face-centred convention), so the design stays inside the
characterized ranges and does not require any factor to be set beyond an edge that has been
justified. Every screening factor was carried into the response-surface stage, because each
was active on at least one response. The design adds the quadratic terms to the screening
model and supports prediction inside the region. The full matrix and the measured responses are given
in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

A-Mab concentration was assessed one factor at a time across its full range with the
kinetic factors at their set-points. It was excluded from the multivariate designs for the
reason given in the risk section above. Its expected mechanism is a matrix effect on the
acid titration, and it does not enter the inactivation kinetics as a term of its own.
Adding it to the multivariate design would have doubled the run count for a factor with no
expected interaction. The outcome of the assessment is reported with the parameter
classification below.

# Results

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

The step is highly reproducible in the two product quality responses and considerably less
so in the log reduction factor. The `{python} cp_rsm` replicate centre points of the
response-surface design give the reproducibility shown in @tbl-centre.

The log reduction factor is by far the least precise response, at

`{python} f"{cv_r.loc[L_AGG, '%CV']:.2f}"` % for the pool aggregate. In absolute terms the
replicate standard deviation of the log reduction factor is

of the infectivity assay is `{python} f"{amv_3017_precision:.2f}"` log₁₀ for a single

## Mechanistic interpretation

The surfaces have the shape the underlying chemistry predicts, and that agreement is part
of the evidence for the step. Acid inactivation of an enveloped virus is a denaturation
reaction. Its rate rises as the pH falls further below the stability limit of the envelope
glycoproteins and as the temperature rises, and the extent achieved is the rate integrated
over the hold. A model in which pH, hold time and temperature act additively on a
logarithmic measure of survival is what that mechanism predicts, and it is what the
coefficients show. No coupling between the three factors was demonstrated over the ranges
studied, so the main effects and the quadratic term in pH describe the surfaces adequately.
Any curvature in the boundary of the operating region comes from that quadratic term in pH,
and not from two factors acting together.

Aggregate formation is driven by the same acid exposure acting on the antibody instead of
on the virus, and the species formed are dimer and higher order (SEC-HPLC). It responds
differently, though, tracking hold time and temperature while staying flat in pH across the
band studied. The likely reason is that the antibody is already below the pH of its
acid-labile conformational transition even at the top of the range studied, so a further
reduction in pH changes the exposure very little. That is consistent
with the platform history, in which the low-pH hold has been operated across this band for
three prior products without an aggregate problem.

Deamidation behaves as a simple time-dependent chemical modification. The acidic charge
variant level rises with hold time alone, and across the whole characterization range for
hold time it rises by `{python} f"{acv_span:.2f}"` percentage points, from
`{python} f"{acv_hold_lo:.2f}"` % at the shortest hold to
`{python} f"{acv_hold_hi:.2f}"` % at the longest, against an acceptance limit of
`{python} f"{acv_hi:.0f}"` %. The attribute is real, the mechanism is understood, and the
magnitude is negligible against its criterion.

The practical consequence of these three mechanisms is that the step cannot be described by
independent ranges on its parameters. Clearance and aggregate move in opposite directions
with hold time, and clearance depends on the combination of pH, hold time and temperature
rather than on any one of them. A multivariate region is therefore needed, and it is
defined in the next section.

# Design space {#sec-designspace}

The design space of the step is the part of the characterized cube in which the predicted
XMuLV log reduction factor meets the required step contribution and both product quality
responses stay within their drug substance limits. The two product quality constraints are
inactive. Over the whole characterized cube the fitted model predicts a pool aggregate of
at most `{python} f"{agg_max:.2f}"` % against a limit of `{python} f"{agg_hi:.0f}"` %, and
an acidic charge variant level of at most `{python} f"{acv_max:.2f}"` % against a limit of
`{python} f"{acv_hi:.0f}"` %. The highest pool aggregate measured in either design was
`{python} f"{agg_obs_max:.2f}"` % (@tbl-appa-resp and @tbl-appb-resp), which is also far
below the limit. Neither attribute constrains the region anywhere inside the ranges
studied. The binding constraint is viral clearance.

The clearance constraint binds at one corner. The least favourable combination for
clearance is the highest pH studied with the shortest hold and the lowest temperature, and
there the fitted model predicts `{python} f"{lrf_corner:.2f}"` log₁₀ against a required
step contribution of `{python} f"{lrf_lo:.2f}"` log₁₀. The corner fails in the model, and
it failed in the executed data. At that corner, `{python} n_below` runs returned measured
log reduction factors below the requirement, the lowest being
`{python} f"{lrf_corner_min:.2f}"` log₁₀. The predicted shortfall of
`{python} f"{lrf_short:.2f}"` log₁₀ is small in absolute terms, and it is much smaller
than the residual standard error of the model, which is
`{python} f"{fit_r['xmulv_lrf']['rmse']:.2f}"` log₁₀. A shortfall inside the noise cannot
be argued away as noise, because the same argument would prevent the corner from being
declared acceptable. The corner is excluded.

Holding the shortest hold time and the lowest temperature, the model meets the requirement
up to pH `{python} f"{ph_eof:.2f}"`, so the excluded region is a thin slice at the top of
the pH range and only when both of the other factors are also at their least favourable
edge. At the set-point hold time and temperature the requirement is met across the whole pH
range. The design space is therefore the characterized cube less that corner, and its
principal plane is pH against hold time, which is the plane shown in @fig-contours.
Temperature shifts the surface without changing its shape.

The normal operating ranges lie well inside this region. At the set-point the model
predicts `{python} f"{lrf_sp:.2f}"` log₁₀, and at the least favourable corner of the
normal operating ranges it predicts `{python} f"{lrf_nor:.2f}"` log₁₀, a margin of
`{python} f"{lrf_nor_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ over the requirement. The normal operating
ranges sit inside the design space, and the design space sits inside the knowledge space
bounded by the characterization ranges of @tbl-params.

Three bounds apply to this claim. It holds only over the characterized ranges of the three
factors and only for feed material within the platform specification for Protein A eluate,
since the feed was not varied in these designs. It is a claim about mean predicted
responses from a fitted model, so the reliability at the boundary of the region is lower
than it is at the centre, and it should not be read as an assurance figure for an
individual batch. It rests on the qualified scale-down model, and, as for every viral
clearance claim, the clearance itself has been demonstrated only at small scale. Movement
within the region is not a change in the regulatory sense of ICH Q8, although it remains
subject to the pharmaceutical quality system. Movement outside the region requires a change
control assessment and, where the excluded corner is concerned, new data.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

The design space is a multivariate statement. The proven acceptable ranges complement it
with a per attribute, per parameter view, and they answer a narrower question about how
far one parameter can be moved before the attribute it governs leaves acceptance. The
acceptance
basis differs between the attributes. For the pool aggregate and the acidic charge variants
it is the drug substance specification given in @tbl-cqa. For XMuLV it is the contribution
this step must make to the cumulative claim, which is the cumulative requirement less the
clearance credited to the other steps, and it is `{python} f"{lrf_lo:.2f}"` log₁₀.

Two analyses were run for every attribute and parameter pair, and both are given in
@tbl-par. The first holds the other parameters fixed and scans the parameter of interest
across its characterization range on a grid, using the fitted response-surface model. The
second varies the other parameters within their normal operating ranges by Monte-Carlo of
the same model, and takes the range over which the 95 % predictive interval stays within
acceptance. The second is a robustness criterion and is the narrower of the two by
construction.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.par_table(UO))
```

: Proven acceptable ranges by attribute and parameter, with the characterization range for
comparison. {#tbl-par}

For the pool aggregate and the acidic charge variants the two analyses agree with each
other and with the characterization range, for every parameter. The whole studied
range of every parameter is proven acceptable for those two attributes, and it stays
acceptable when the other two parameters move within their normal operating ranges. That is
a strong robustness result, and it is bounded by the ranges in the third column of
@tbl-par. Nothing is claimed beyond them.

For XMuLV clearance the two analyses agree for hold time and for temperature, and they
differ for pH. The whole hold time range and the whole temperature range are proven
acceptable under both analyses, which is expected, since both factors raise clearance as
they increase and their lower edges were included in the region only in combination with a
high pH. The pH range narrows under the second analysis, from the full characterization
range to an upper edge of `{python} f"{par_nor_ph[1]:.2f}"`. XMuLV clearance is the binding
attribute, and the residual margin is `{python} f"{ph_par_headroom:.2f}"` pH units above
the upper edge of the normal operating range for pH. In other words, pH would have to be
run above its control band, with hold time and temperature simultaneously unfavourable
inside their own control bands, before the predictive interval touched the requirement.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-lrf
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range of inactivation pH for the XMuLV log reduction factor. The acceptable region is shaded green, the acceptance limit is drawn, and the set-point and normal operating range are marked."
_ = D.fig_par(UO, "xmulv_lrf", D.governing_factor(UO, "xmulv_lrf"))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-agg
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range of hold time for the pool aggregate level."
_ = D.fig_par(UO, "aggregate_out_pct", D.governing_factor(UO, "aggregate_out_pct"))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-acv
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range of hold time for the acidic charge variant level."
_ = D.fig_par(UO, "acidic_variants", D.governing_factor(UO, "acidic_variants"))
plt.show()
```

Each governed attribute is plotted against its governing parameter, which is the parameter
with the largest main effect on it in the response-surface model. @fig-par-lrf shows XMuLV
clearance against pH, and the two panels show how much the acceptable region contracts when
hold time and temperature are allowed to vary within their control bands. @fig-par-agg and
@fig-par-acv show the pool aggregate and the acidic charge variants against hold time, and
in both cases the acceptable region covers the whole studied range with a wide margin to
the limit.

These ranges and the design space answer different questions, and the two are not
interchangeable. A proven acceptable range is a one-dimensional
statement about a single parameter. The design space is the multivariate region, and it is
the smaller claim wherever the parameters interact or, as here, wherever the attribute
depends on a combination of them. The pH range is the only case in this step where a
univariate range binds at all, and even there the corner excluded from the design space is
excluded by the combination of all three factors and not by pH alone. The binding constraint on
the operating region is therefore the design-space corner described above, not any
univariate proven acceptable range. Both statements are bounded by the characterization
ranges and by the fitted model.

# Parameter classification

Each parameter was classified against the decision logic of SOP-4001, which combines the
demonstrated effect on a CQA with the risk that the parameter leaves the design space in
routine operation. The outcome is given in the last column of @tbl-params and the reasoning
is set out below.

- Inactivation pH is a critical process parameter. It carries the largest effect on the
  attribute this step sets, its control band is narrow relative to the characterized range,
  and it is the parameter that defines the excluded corner of the design space. Values
  above the studied range have not been shown to inactivate XMuLV within the shortest
  acceptable hold, so the consequence of an excursion in the unfavourable direction is a
  loss of clearance rather than a loss of product quality.
- Hold time is a well-controlled critical process parameter. It has a significant effect on
  all three responses, and it is the only parameter that moves clearance and product
  quality in opposite directions. It is classified below pH because it is set by a timer
  against a controlled clock (the distributed control system record), its whole
  characterized range is proven acceptable for every attribute, and the risk of leaving the design space through hold time alone is very low.
- Temperature is a well-controlled critical process parameter. Its effect on clearance is
  significant but is the smallest of the three
  (`{python} f"{eff_s['xmulv_lrf'].loc['C', 'Effect']:+.2f}"` log₁₀ across the whole
  characterized range), and its effect on aggregate is likewise smaller than that of hold
  time. It is held by a jacketed vessel within a band far narrower than the range studied.
- A-Mab concentration is a general process parameter. The univariate assessment covered the
  full range over which Protein A eluate is delivered, and no effect on a quality attribute
  governed by this step was demonstrated, so the whole delivered range is proven acceptable
  (@tbl-params). That null result is retained in the knowledge space as evidence that the
  step tolerates the whole delivered concentration range, and it is the reason the parameter
  needs no control beyond the routine monitoring already applied to the eluate.

Two further classification points follow from the results. No parameter of this step is a
key process parameter, because none of them drives step yield or another process
performance measure independently of the quality attributes above. The absence of any
significant interaction in either design means that no parameter is classified on the
strength of a combination effect. Every classification above rests on a main effect
demonstrated in its own right.

# Contribution to the control strategy

The step contributes four elements to the control strategy for the drug substance.

Parameter control is the first. Inactivation pH is controlled to the normal operating range
in @tbl-params and verified by an independent probe before the hold clock starts, which is
the in-process control that protects the clearance claim. Hold time is controlled to its
normal operating range with a minimum of `{python} f"{P['hold_time'].nor[0]:.0f}"` minutes,
and temperature to its normal operating range. A-Mab concentration is monitored and not
controlled to a range narrower than the eluate specification.

Record integrity is the second, and it arises from one of the deviations described below.
The hold time recorded by the distributed control system is the controlled record for the
step, the manual log is a secondary record, and clock synchronisation between the two is
verified before execution. A discrepancy between them is treated as a deviation regardless
of magnitude.

Monitoring and release testing are the third. The neutralised pool is tested for aggregate
by SEC-HPLC (AMV-3011) and the drug substance is tested for charge variants by icIEF
(AMV-3013), so both attributes this step affects are covered by release testing further
down the process.
Life-cycle control is the fourth, and it has two parts. The scale-down spiking model is
requalified on the schedule set by SOP-1001, and the parameter ranges above enter continued
process verification at commercial scale.

The step does not deliver viral safety on its own. Its XMuLV increment is one of three
credited contributions (@tbl-vc), and it makes no contribution at all to the parvovirus
claim, which rests on the anion exchange step (PCR-008) and the small-virus retentive
filtration step (PCR-009). The enveloped-virus contributions are credited separately
because their mechanisms are independent, and the cumulative claim is consolidated in
PCMR-001. Aggregate control is shared with the cation exchange step (PCR-007), which
reduces the level this step delivers.

# Discussion

The step is well understood and its behaviour matches the mechanism assumed for it. The
kinetic factors (pH, hold time and temperature) act additively on the log reduction factor,
two of them act on aggregate, one of them acts on deamidation, and no interaction was found
in either design. The
operating region follows directly from those relationships, and the only boundary that
binds is the clearance requirement at the corner where the highest pH meets the shortest
hold and the lowest temperature. Prior knowledge from three earlier products predicted this
structure, and the study confirmed it rather than revising it.

The adverse finding of the study is that corner, where `{python} n_below` executed runs
returned log reduction factors below the contribution required of the step. The fitted
model agrees that the corner fails. The mitigating evidence is that the corner requires all three factors to be
at their least favourable edge at once, that the normal operating ranges are far from it,
and that the predicted margin at the least favourable corner of those ranges is
`{python} f"{lrf_nor_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀. The residual position is that the corner is
excluded from the design space and the step is not operated there.

Confidence in the scale-down model is high for the operating ranges and is necessarily
qualified for the clearance claim. The hold is a homogeneous reaction in which the
controlling variables are scale-independent, so the model reproduces the commercial step by
construction and its qualification confirmed that it does. The clearance data are a
different matter. They are generated with a laboratory virus preparation (a cultured XMuLV stock) spiked
into the feed. The relationship between that preparation and an adventitious contaminant is
an assumption of the method and not a result of this study [@ichq5a]. That assumption is common
to every modular clearance claim and is managed by the conservatism built into the
requirement.

Three further limitations should be recorded. The response-surface model for the log
reduction factor has a low predicted coefficient of determination, because the infectivity
assay contributes a large part of the observed variance, and it should be read as a model
of mean behaviour and not as a batch-level assurance statement. The design space has not
been confirmed at commercial scale at the edges of the ranges, which is a general property
of characterization work and is addressed by Stage 2. The acidic charge variant response
returned no replicate variation in either design, so the study bounds the magnitude of the
deamidation increment but provides no useful estimate of its variability.

The study recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations, and both were dispositioned as retained.
Neither changed a fitted effect, a parameter classification or the operating region, and both are described
in full in the deviations section below. One of them produced a lasting control, which is
the record integrity element of the control strategy above.

Only one parameter of this step needs the most stringent control. Inactivation pH is
classified as a critical process parameter, and hold time and temperature are
well-controlled critical process parameters, which reflects the ease with which a timer and
a jacket hold their targets compared with the consequence of a titration error.

# Conclusions

The low-pH viral inactivation step is characterized and its operating region is defined.
The step has `{python} n_par` parameters, of which `{python} n_mv` were studied
multivariately and `{python} n_uv` univariately. Inactivation pH is a
critical process parameter, hold time and temperature are well-controlled critical process
parameters, and A-Mab concentration is a general process parameter.

The response-surface models define a region covering the characterized ranges of pH, hold
time and temperature, less the corner that combines the highest pH with the shortest hold
and the lowest temperature. Within that region the XMuLV log reduction factor meets the
step contribution of `{python} f"{lrf_lo:.2f}"` log₁₀ required by the cumulative claim,
the pool aggregate stays below `{python} f"{agg_hi:.0f}"` % and the acidic charge variants
stay below `{python} f"{acv_hi:.0f}"` %. The normal operating ranges lie inside the region
with a predicted clearance margin of `{python} f"{lrf_nor_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ at their
least favourable corner.

At commercial scale the cumulative XMuLV clearance has a one-sided Cpk of
`{python} f"{xmulv_cpk:.2f}"` and a margin of `{python} f"{xmulv_margin:.2f}"` log₁₀ to
its requirement, which is the tightest of the attributes this step governs. The study
recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations, and both were resolved without changing a fitted
effect, a parameter classification or the reported operating region. The
step assures a defined enveloped-virus inactivation increment within bounded product
quality cost. It does not assure the viral safety of the drug substance by itself, and it
makes no parvovirus claim. The findings roll up into PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan

The study recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations during execution. Each was investigated,
its root cause was established, its impact on the reported results was assessed, and both
were dispositioned as retained. The register is given in @tbl-dev and
each is described below.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
```

: Deviations recorded during execution of PCR-006. {#tbl-dev}

Both entries in @tbl-dev were found after the affected runs were complete, one at
batch-record reconciliation and one at assay review. Neither was detected by an
in-process control at the time it occurred. The two post-execution checks that did find
them are part of the study record, and both are described below.

## DEV-006-01: hold-time record discrepancy

The recorded hold time for one run differed between two sources by
`{python} dev_006_01_time_discrepancy_min` minutes. The distributed control system trend
and the manual batch record disagreed, and the discrepancy was found during batch-record
reconciliation after the run was complete. Until it was resolved, the hold time actually
applied to that run was uncertain by that margin.

The investigation compared the timestamps of the two systems against a reference clock and
found an offset between the distributed control system clock and the local panel clock used
by the operator. The distributed control system record was confirmed as the accurate one
and as the controlled record for the step. No equipment fault was found, and no other run
of either design was affected.

The impact on the study is negligible on two grounds. The uncertainty of
`{python} dev_006_01_time_discrepancy_min` minutes is small against the characterization
range for hold time, which spans
`{python} f"{P['hold_time'].prange[0]:.0f}"` to
`{python} f"{P['hold_time'].prange[1]:.0f}"` minutes, so the run sits inside the studied
range under either record. The effect of that uncertainty on the response is smaller still.
Evaluating the fitted model at the set-point and again
`{python} dev_006_01_time_discrepancy_min` minutes later changes the predicted log
reduction factor by `{python} f"{dev_hold_shift:.3f}"` log₁₀, which is an order of
magnitude below the residual standard error of the model
(`{python} f"{fit_r['xmulv_lrf']['rmse']:.2f}"` log₁₀). The run was retained with the
distributed control system value, and the fitted effects are unchanged. The deviation
produced the record integrity control described in the control strategy section above.

## DEV-006-02: infectivity assay cytotoxicity at low dilution

The sample matrix was cytotoxic to the indicator cell line at the lowest dilutions of the
infectivity titration, so those wells could not be scored. The finding was made at assay
review of the titration records. Titres for the affected samples were calculated
from a dilution of one in `{python} dev_006_02_cytotox_dilution` and above, following the
cytotoxicity provisions of AMV-3017. Excluding the lowest dilutions raises the effective
quantitation limit for those samples by `{python} f"{cytotox_offset:.2f}"` log₁₀ above the
validated limit of `{python} f"{amv_3017_loq:.1f}"` log₁₀ TCID50/mL.

The root cause is the sample matrix itself. The post-hold samples are at low pH and carry
the acid titrant, and both are toxic to the indicator cells at low dilution. This is a
known property of low-pH hold samples and is the reason AMV-3017 carries a cytotoxicity
control. No assay fault and no sample handling error were identified.

The consequence for the reported data is a conservative bias in one direction only. Where
a post-hold titre could not be resolved below the raised quantitation limit, the log
reduction factor reported for that run is a minimum, so the true clearance is at least the
value used in the analysis. A bias of that sign cannot create an apparent clearance that
does not exist, and it cannot mask a failing corner, since it can only make a reported
value too small. The centre-point reproducibility of the assay across
`{python} cp_rsm` replicate runs, at `{python} f"{cv_r.loc[L_LRF, 'SD']:.2f}"` log₁₀,
remains consistent with the validated intermediate precision of the method. The affected
results were retained and the analysis was not repeated.
